expectations.text: Calculates current monthly handling cost as $21,600 and, conditional on genuine 50% time savings, gross monthly capacity value as $10,800 and net recurring value before other costs as $4,800; does not label capacity savings guaranteed cash savings.
expectations.evidence: Calculates 480 hours/month, $21,600 current cost and $10,800 capacity value, explicitly distinguishing capacity from cash. Gives correct first-year residual and 7.5-month payback, but never states the requested $4,800 net recurring monthly value.

expectations.text: Identifies selection bias and exclusion of missing-document claims in the 80-case demo, and does not treat 94% agreement with historical decisions as validated live accuracy or correctness.

expectations.text: Proposes an evaluation that includes missing-document cases and measures total adjuster review/correction time plus approval and denial errors separately, retaining human decision authority during the experiment.
expectations.evidence: Requires natural missing-document prevalence and inspection changes; measures total handling, follow-up, inspection, review and correction time; separately reports incorrect approvals and denials; keeps outputs in shadow mode and an adjuster approving every decision.

expectations.text: Makes any larger investment conditional on measured results and compares the structured-form alternative or a combined approach without assuming its adoption or declaring AI categorically required or unsuitable.
expectations.evidence: Advance only if representative held-out results meet tolerances and measured net value covers complete costs. Compares structured intake against existing handling and assistance, explicitly calling adoption and avoided work unknown.

ambiguous_criteria: The economics assertion is failed only for omission of explicit $4,800/month net recurring value. Correct 7.5-month implementation recovery and $21,600 first-year residual imply that value, so a rubric accepting implicit calculation could reasonably pass it.

poor_reasoning: The sentence saying cash savings require reduced overtime/hiring/staffing costs “or valuable redeployment” conflates monetizable capacity benefit with cash savings: redeployment alone need not reduce cash expenditure. The surrounding capacity caveat still satisfies the assertion.
